title: Special Report: American Higher Education Is Going Broke
author: Anthony Bradley
summary: Anthony Bradley's special report argues that American higher education is in the early stages of a slow-motion financial collapse obscured by the cultural prestige of football Saturdays and luxury amenities. Public higher education debt grew more than 85% between 2007 and 2017, and institutions continued borrowing during the low-interest-rate years to fund athletics facilities and administrative expansion. Now the demographic cliff is arriving simultaneously: fewer students, massive institutional debt, and rising interest rates are a lethal combination for undercapitalized institutions. Bradley argues universities built their financial models on assumptions -- perpetual enrollment growth, low interest rates, strong endowment returns -- none of which hold today. The true institutional debt load is estimated between $400 billion and $500 billion. The institutions most at risk are regional comprehensives and mid-tier schools without large endowments or elite brand recognition.
points: * Public higher education debt surged more than 85% between 2007 and 2017, making it the fastest-growing category of municipal debt during that period. * The demographic cliff is arriving simultaneously with the debt crisis: fewer traditional-age students, massive institutional debt, and rising interest rates are a lethal combination. * Universities built financial models on assumptions -- perpetual enrollment growth, low interest rates, strong endowment returns -- none of which hold in the current environment. * Regional comprehensive universities and mid-tier institutions face the sharpest risk: they lack the endowments and brand power of elite institutions to weather demographic and financial shocks. * The visible collapse is lagging because debt-financed amenities maintain the appearance of institutional health even as academic programs and financial reserves deteriorate.
quotes: America, I do not think people fully understand how bad this situation has become.
The higher education system is starting to resemble a slow-motion financial collapse hidden behind football Saturdays, luxury dorms, and smiling admissions brochures.
Someone recently said, "College is dead." After digging into the numbers, I am starting to think they may be right.

It exploded to 4.2 million views, which made me realize people can sense something breaking beneath the surface of American life.
